title: Canonical adjunction transposes of exact degree-zero insertions
statement: For abelian categories $V,W$ with chosen derived categories, an exact additive functor $R:W\to V$, an adjunction $L\dashv D(R)$ and an ordinary insertion $\eta:F\to R(G)$, define $\operatorname{adjointInsertion}(\eta)$ as the adjunction transpose of $\operatorname{single}(\eta)$ followed by the inverse exact-single comparison [def-geo-exact-degree-zero-interface]. These are constructed arrows, not chosen witnesses. Compatible ordinary insertions compose under the canonical left-adjoint compositor. An insertion representing the unbounded Hom bijections has invertible transpose. Specializations to an essentially small module site use exactly its existing restriction functor and chosen adjunction.

proof.text: Construct adjointInsertion by the actual adjunction hom equivalence on the exact-single insertion. For composition apply exact unit_comp, unfold its generic named presentation, and transpose the composite through the composed adjunction. The mate identity for leftAdjointCompIso supplies the specified comparison.
Universal_iff identifies the Hom bijections with the raw insertion. Postcompose with the adjunction hom equivalence and use its naturality. The coyoneda bijection criterion proves invertibility.

Specialize the generic construction and theorems at an essentially small site with module sheaves, fixing the coefficient restriction and its actual chosen adjunction in each definition. Unfold only the named scalar universal predicate to apply the generic criterion. No new choices or witness data are added.

def adjointInsertion
    {V W : Type*} [Category V] [Category W] [Abelian V] [Abelian W]
    [HasDerivedCategory V] [HasDerivedCategory W]
    (R : W ⥤ V) [R.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits R] [PreservesFiniteColimits R]
    {L : DerivedCategory V ⥤ DerivedCategory W} (a : L ⊣ R.mapDerivedCategory)
    {F : V} {G : W} (η : F ⟶ R.obj G) :
    L.obj ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor V 0).obj F) ⟶
      (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor W 0).obj G
